description: Detection-as-Code (app/services/detection_as_code) scenarios. The runner does NOT create a second rule engine and does NOT modify the shipped rule inventory. It uses the real LifecycleService against a temporary rules root seeded with one synthetic YARA rule, exactly like backend/scripts/detection_as_code_e2e.py, so the shipped 53-rule manifest stays byte-identical. Every version bump, release, deploy and rollback is persisted to PostgreSQL through the real repository and audited.
controlled_root: temporary directory (never the shipped app/services/detection/rules root)
shipped_manifest: app/services/detection/rules/manifest.yaml (53 rules; hash-verified, never rewritten by this dataset)

rule_under_test.purpose: Synthetic rule whose condition is a unique marker string, so a positive and a negative fixture can be proven to behave differently.

scenarios.purpose: LifecycleService.validate_rule performs the full gate chain: manifest entry, source file, path traversal, source hash, secret scan, rule type, severity, metadata, compile, positive fixture, negative fixture. Any failure fails closed and nothing is released.
LifecycleService.release moves the validated version into a release record.
LifecycleService.deploy marks the release deployed; the version then becomes visible in LifecycleService.build_deployed_registry().
build_deployed_registry verifies every deployed release (validated state + on-disk source hash) and refuses to build a partial set - it fails closed.
The real YaraDetectionEngine compiles the deployed source and matches the positive fixture bytes; the negative fixture must not match.
A 1.1.0 edit to the same rule produces a new version row with a new source hash; releasing and deploying it changes the active registry.
LifecycleService.rollback returns the active deployment to 1.0.0 and records the change with rollback_from set.
